questions.question: She said she would have left earlier, but she didn’t know the train schedule well enough. What does this sentence imply about her attitude?
options: She was very confident about leaving early.
She regretted not leaving sooner due to uncertainty.
She deliberately waited for the last train.
She had already left before the train arrived.
questions.answer: She regretted not leaving sooner due to uncertainty.

questions.question: The report *had been written* by the team last week, but it was only published today. Which form of the passive voice is used correctly?
options: The report was written by the team last week.
The report had been written by the team last week.
The report was being written by the team last week.
The report was being written by the team by the team last week.
questions.answer: The report had been written by the team last week.

questions.question: If you *hadn’t* spent so much time studying, you would have passed the exam. What type of conditional is this?
options: Zero conditional
First conditional
Second conditional
Third conditional

questions.question: The manager suggested that we *should start* the project immediately to meet the deadline. Which prepositional phrase best fits the sentence?
options: The manager suggested that we should start the project at once.
The manager suggested that we should start the project by tomorrow.
The manager suggested that we should start the project in the morning.
The manager suggested that we should start the project within the week.
questions.answer: The manager suggested that we should start the project at once.

questions.question: She *used to play* football every weekend, but now she prefers to spend her time reading. Which collocation is most appropriate here?
options: She used to play football in the weekends.
She used to play football on the weekends.
She used to play football at the weekends.
She used to play football during the weekends.
questions.answer: She used to play football on the weekends.

questions.question: The children were so excited that they couldn’t stop talking. Which discourse marker best fits here to show a contrast?
options: However, they were still excited.
On the other hand, they were tired.
Instead, they started playing outside.
Nevertheless, they kept chatting loudly.
questions.answer: On the other hand, they were tired.

questions.question: The news *spread* through the village quickly because everyone knew each other. Which dependent preposition is most appropriate in this context?
options: The news spread among the villagers because everyone knew each other.
The news spread to the villagers because everyone knew each other.
The news spread by the villagers because everyone knew each other.
The news spread with the villagers because everyone knew each other.
questions.answer: The news spread among the villagers because everyone knew each other.

questions.question: She was so disappointed that she *almost gave up*. Which lexical choice best fits the context of strong emotion?
options: She gave up completely.
She decided to continue.
She stopped working for a while.
She left without saying goodbye.

questions.question: The company *relied on* the new software to improve productivity. Which collocation best fits this sentence?
options: The company relied on the software to improve productivity.
The company relied in the software to improve productivity.
The company relied at the software to improve productivity.
The company relied by the software to improve productivity.
questions.answer: The company relied on the software to improve productivity.

questions.question: If she *hadn’t been so tired*, she *would have finished* the report by now. Which of the following correctly combines these two sentences?
options: Because she was tired, she couldn’t finish the report.
Since she was tired, she wouldn’t have finished the report.
Having been tired, she couldn’t finish the report.
If she had been tired, she would have finished the report.
questions.answer: Because she was tired, she couldn’t finish the report.
